fixes.action: Print the board-approved incident sheet for the office and warehouse walls, and save a copy where both admins can reach it offline.
Remove the warehouse router's port forward to the NAS, and confirm from a phone off the warehouse network that the login page no longer answers.
Update the NAS firmware, turn on its automatic security updates, and give each shift lead a named account in place of the shared admin password.
Turn on NAS snapshots and set the cloud-backup service to keep at least 30 days of earlier versions, so an encrypted sync can be rolled back.
Change the hosting account's SFTP password, then turn SFTP off; the web volunteer turns it on for a session when a file change is needed.
Delete the design agency's two CMS admin accounts and require two-step sign-in for the three that remain.
Roll the processor's secret API key, replace it with a restricted key that can only create checkout sessions, and note the rotation date in the web volunteer's records.
Block sign-in on donations@ and info@, and give the triage volunteers delegated access through accounts of their own.
Remove the e-signature add-in if the grant agreement is closed, and turn on the admin consent request flow so the operations manager approves any new app.
Write to the former managed IT provider asking which tools, integrations and accounts it connected to the tenant, and when each was removed; file the reply.
Search the tenant's audit log from Oct 1 for new inbox rules, forwarding and app consents touching donations@ and info@, plus anything the former provider names.
Run one Purview audit search for this month's donations@ activity to prove audit is recording, and write the retention period into the operations manager's records.
Limit the scheduling app's roster so volunteers see first names and shifts only; mobile numbers go to shift leads and the volunteer coordinator.
Send the tenant's alert emails to a security@ list read by both admins, and remove the mail rule that files them away.
Ask the donor-management vendor what export limits and bulk-export alerts it offers, and turn on whatever it has for the development director.
Replace the warehouse camera with one that records to the NAS only and has no cloud viewer.
